title: Loop back: spot the right tool fast
idea: LOOP (review). Rapid mixed recognition across all laps — read a tiny snippet or a phrase and name what it does or which tool fits.

options: How many numbers are negative (count with a condition)
exercises.explanation: A counter that grows only when x < 0 counts the negatives. Reading the shape tells you the pattern.
Seed with the first, update on anything larger — the max pattern by hand. Recognizing it at a glance is the goal.

exercises.prompt: Phrase: 'show the running total of a list'. Which tool?
options: A loop with an accumulator starting at 0
exercises.explanation: A running total is an accumulator: total = 0, then add each item in a loop. No sum() in this course.

exercises.prompt: Phrase: 'return 1 if a number is even, else 0'. Which tool?
options: A helper with if/else using the remainder (% 2 == 0)
exercises.explanation: Even means n % 2 == 0. A decision helper returns 1 or 0 — conditions (Lap 2) plus the % operator (Lap 0).

exercises.prompt: Match each snippet idea to its pattern.

pairs.left: total = total + x in a loop

exercises.explanation: Each tiny shape is a signature of one pattern. Fast recognition speeds up both writing and debugging.

exercises.prompt: What does len(nums) give, and what must it NOT be used for?
options: It gives the SIZE of the list; do not use it to add the list up
It gives the total; use it instead of a sum loop
exercises.explanation: len is the count of items — allowed for size. Summing is done by hand with a loop, never by a builtin.

exercises.prompt: A helper that returns a value can be composed into another call; one that only prints cannot.
exercises.explanation: Yes. return feeds the next step; print just shows. Composition needs returned values.

exercises.prompt: Phrase: 'the average, guarding an empty list'. Which parts?
options: Empty guard, then sum for the total, then divide by len
exercises.explanation: Average = total / count, with an empty guard first so you never divide by 0. Several laps combine in one small helper.

exercises.prompt: Phrase: 'keep only the passing scores'. Which tool?
options: A filter: empty list, append scores that pass
exercises.explanation: Keeping a subset is a filter — build a new list of the items that pass the test.

options: Recognizing patterns and tools quickly lets you break any problem into parts you already know how to solve
Every problem needs a brand-new idea
Patterns are impossible to tell apart
len can replace a sum loop
exercises.explanation: Fast recognition is the payoff of all the laps. Once you see the pattern in a part, you know the helper to write.
